text:
The episode of Dragons’ Den Vio Sara Davies and Touker Suleyman block horns in a tense battle for a travel team company in which they both wanted to invest.
Entrepreneur Hayley Hanigan, from London, went to the BBC show with the hope of obtaining an investment in his business, Tiny Explorers.
As a four -year -old mother, she could relate to the purchase of costly travel equipment for her children that she would only use once or twice, such as car seats and cribs.
Then came the idea of ​​establishing a company where parents can rent equipment at a cheaper pace than buying it, without the discomfort of moving it with them.
He asked dragon for an investment of £ 50,000 in exchange for 10 percent of the corporation.
Tiny Explorers gave more than £ 203,000 in its first year and then £ 288,000 in her second year, and the businesswoman added that she works with hotels in London who reserve teams for tourists who stay with them.
Hayley said they have more than 100 articles on their website that can be rented, and added that the PVP of a folding walking chair is £ 450, but it would only cost £ 50 per week rent it.
While Deborah Meaden, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett retired, Sara Davies and Touker Suleyman stayed fighting for who would reach an agreement with Hayley.

Sara, who is the mother of two children, Charlie and Oliver, offered Hayley exactly what she asked for, what Steven said it was a “brilliant offer.”
However, Touker then revealed that he was also interested in Hayley’s business, but he would like to take him along the route of offering short -term services.
The businessman said: ‘You have a very good offer, but is it the right offer? Is it a mentor you want or is it someone who can help you strategically? That’s where I enter.
‘I have all those real estate agents in London, I have a relationship. But it has a price. I will not do it for 10 percent.
